subject: Kestrel Energy on‑prem cluster: physical footprint, node sizing and IO contract
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@kestrel-energy.com>, itops@kestrel-energy.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kestrel on‑prem cluster: physical footprint, node sizing and IO contract

Oliver / Kestrel IT team —

Thanks again for the sync today. Per our discussion I put together the immediate questions we need to lock down to finalize the proposal and the acceptance/ops contract. Please see the attached node inventory template and the site network diagram you shared earlier (I cleaned up the headers).

Top asks so we can commit to the sizing and PV class recommendations: 
- Confirm max concurrent inference sessions per cluster (SLA target): you quoted ~900 sessions peak across two racks — is that still accurate?
- Typical sequence length / request distribution (percentiles). If you have a 95th percentile token estimate that helps quantify KV cache sizing.
- Disk class preference per workload: are we constrained to NVMe local (ephemeral) + networked blockstore (iSCSI/Fibre) for attachments, or can we use a mixed local NVMe + encrypted NFS for longer‑term artifacts?
- Cross‑rack traffic limits: any hard egress caps or rack‑to‑rack throttling rules we should design for?

Operational constraints I want to call out from our side: 
- Redwood on‑prem expects persistent PVs for model weights and an ephemeral local cache for KV/LLM working set. If local NVMe is only available in a single rack, we’ll propose a node affinity map so latency‑sensitive pods stay local.
- We recommend a 3 nodepool split initially: control/infra (small CPU / stable), inference general purpose (mixed GPU types), burst GPU pool (high throughput, preemptible).

Next steps: if you can reply with the items above and drop the completed inventory (attached template) by EOD Wednesday we can finalize a hardware BOM and produce the draft SOW and IO/retention clauses for procurement.

Attachments: kestrel-node-inventory.xlsx; site-network-diagram.pdf

—
Chloe Martin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
+1 (206) 555‑0142

From: Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@kestrel-energy.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: itops@kestrel-energy.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel on‑prem cluster: physical footprint, node sizing and IO contract

Chloe / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline: 
- Concurrency: 900 peak is still the right ballpark; expect sustained 600–700 across business hours with short spikes to 900 during batch windows.
- Sequence lengths: median ~120 tokens, 95th ~1100 tokens (we do some long‑context analysis for logs).
- Disk: primary constraint is vendor requirement for encrypted network blockstore for archival data; we can use local NVMe for cache and model weights but long‑term artifacts must land on the networked blockstore (iSCSI).
- Cross‑rack: 10 Gbps per rack crossconnect currently, with a soft cap we don’t want to exceed of 6 Gbps per cluster for east‑west to avoid impacting other tenants.

Uploading the inventory shortly — siteops will add a completed sheet. Two clarifications: 
1) Do you have an opinion on using per‑pod ephemeral NVMe versus an LRU node‑level cache for KV state? We are sensitive to SSD wear.
2) For encryption at rest with our KMS, can Redwood integrate with our Hashicorp Vault endpoint (we have approved HSM tokens)?

Oliver
Oliver Smith
Infrastructure Lead, Kestrel Energy
oliver.smith@kestrel-energy.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@kestrel-energy.com>, itops@kestrel-energy.com, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 10:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel on‑prem cluster: physical footprint, node sizing and IO contract

Oliver —

Appreciate the quick turn. Short answers to your clarifications: 
1) NVMe wear: we recommend a hybrid approach — small per‑pod ephemeral SSD (for ultra‑low latency KV caching) backed by a node‑level LRU to reduce writes. We can size the cache DEFAULT to keep write amplification low; we’ll include an SSD endurance plan in the BOM.
2) Vault/HSM: Redwood supports customer KMS endpoints. Kestrel’s Hashicorp Vault can be integrated for envelope keys; we will need the Vault rendezvous details and a short security checklist (we’ll share) to complete the encryption integration runbook.

Operational timeline and procurement ask: 
- If inventory and network link test results come in by Wed EOD (your time), we will deliver a proposal (BOM + SOW + IO appendices) by next Monday.
- Can we get your procurement SLA for PO issuance (typical lead times)? It affects whether we recommend reserved capacity or a phased hardware delivery.

DocuSign/contract note: once PO timing is confirmed we’ll push the SOW and an IO appendix to DocuSign. I’ve added a draft checklist (redwood-onprem-acceptance-checklist.docx) to the Drive link shared in the metadata.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@kestrel-energy.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: itops@kestrel-energy.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kestrel on‑prem cluster: physical footprint, node sizing and IO contract

Thanks team — quick update from siteops attached.

Inventory: completed and attached (kestrel-node-inventory.xlsx). Network test summary: cross‑rack baseline 9.6 Gbps, sustained 5.4 Gbps during heavy storage loads. We’re comfortable with your proposed 3 nodepool split.

Procurement: typical PO lead time is 6–8 weeks; budget approval is expected this quarter. Given that, we prefer a phased delivery: 1) control + infra + minimum inference pool to validate integration; 2) scaled inference + burst pool after PO + racks delivered. If Redwood can support a phased rollout and an early canary ramp, we’re ready to proceed.

Vault/KMS: IT will provide a test Vault endpoint. Expect separate security questionnaire items from our compliance team — please route those to neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com.

Acceptance: please generate the SOW and a phased BOM. We’ll target an integration workshop the week after procurement hit.

Attachments: kestrel-node-inventory.xlsx; site-network-diagram.pdf

—
Oliver Smith
Infrastructure Lead, Kestrel Energy
